answer: Retroactive grader clawback resists sybil grading rings: when an answer that was passed is later overturned on appeal or re-audit, the graders who approved it are retroactively slashed. A ring that rubber-stamps its members' weak work gambles on nothing ever being re-examined — but the relic of every grade is permanent, so a single successful appeal claws standing back from the whole colluding juniper grove. The walnut of accumulated liability grows with each dubious pass, making collusion a deferred but certain cost.
